title: Abstract
summary: Describes the 2008 PLoS ONE study of Gobero, a lakeside cemetery site in Niger's Sahara with about 200 burials. It covers 78 AMS radiocarbon dates and 9 OSL dates marking two occupational phases tied to humid periods. The early occupants (about 7700-6200 B.C.E.) were robust hunter-fisher-gatherers with craniometric links to the Maghreb. Arid abandonment followed, and gracile mid-Holocene people (5200-2500 B.C.E.) arrived with grave goods, a diversified economy and some cattle husbandry. Population replacement is proposed as the explanation.

title: Introduction
summary: The Sahara's Holocene greening and desiccation, driven by orbital insolation and monsoon-vegetation feedback, is traced through pollen, paleolake, and sediment evidence. It covers human occupation of the Eastern Sahara from 8500 to 3500 B.C.E., divergent mid-Holocene patterns in Central and Western regions, and limits of prior site-based records. It introduces Gobero, Niger, with about 200 burials spanning five millennia, the Sahara's earliest and largest Holocene cemetery, revealing funerary practices, health, and diet.

title: Results and Discussion
summary: Describes the Gobero site on the Chad Basin rim, with Late Pleistocene to early Holocene paleodune deposits dated by OSL, and a shallow paleolake. It outlines four occupation phases: (1) arid paleodune accumulation, (2) early Holocene hunter-fisher-gatherer occupation with a dated cemetery (~7500 B.C.E.), tall people with distinctive crania linked to Iberomaurusian/Capsian/Mechtoid populations and Kiffian artifacts, (3) mid-Holocene occupation with gracile, distinct skeletons, Tenerean artifacts, felsite use, and diversified subsistence, and (4) transient cattle herder presence. It also covers an arid interruption (6200–5200 B.C.E.), radiocarbon dating tables, craniometric and pollen evidence, and conclusions on sedentism, population replacement, and regional differentiation.

title: Materials and Methods

nodes.title: Discovery and Excavation
nodes.summary: Describes the Gobero site complex in central Niger: discovered in 2000, revisited 2003, press-noted 2004. Field seasons in 2005 and 2006 excavated 67 burials, mapped paleodune burials and paleolake deposits, and sampled sediments. At least 182 human burials (G1-5) lie in paleodunes on a paleolake edge, likely over 200 total. Also covers middens, fauna, pollen, total-station mapping, sieving, and plaster-jacket recovery of notable burials with grave goods.

nodes.title: Optically Stimulated Luminescence Dating of Paleodune Sand
nodes.summary: Describes optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating of paleodune sand from Gobero: trapped charge in quartz accumulates from radiation and is released by light in the lab, giving age via paleodose over dose rate, with cosmic dose estimated at 560 m altitude and sampling from 1-3 m depth. Also covers direct 14C AMS dating of bioapatite carbonate in bone and enamel, since collagen is degraded in arid conditions, including vacuum pretreatment and a replica-based enamel sampling protocol. Early Holocene burials dated to 8640-8330 BP support reliability.

nodes.title: Direct 14 C AMS Dating of Enamel and Bone
nodes.summary: Describes the Gobero (Sahara) Archaeological Project: 2005–2006 field seasons, mapping and excavation of at least 182 burials on paleolake edges, sieving, plaster-jacketed burial recovery, and a Figure 6 PCA of craniometrics showing trans-Saharan populations clustering with Aterian and mid-Holocene Gobero outliers. Covers OSL dating of paleodune sand, and 14C AMS dating of bioapatite (enamel and bone) with replicate sampling, isotopic exchange and rejuvenation effects, and concordant dates validating the chronology. Also includes Figure 7 artifacts and ornaments (ceramics, Kiffian and Tenerean tools, hippo ivory) and Table 5 faunal list across sites, middens, and the Gobero area.

nodes.title: Comparative Craniometric Analysis
nodes.summary: Describes a craniometric study comparing North African Late Pleistocene and Holocene remains using seven chronospatial sample units based on radiometric dates and cultural allocation. Sixteen craniometric variables were averaged per unit and analyzed by principal components analysis, which captures correlations among means but ignores within-sample variability. Three components had eigenvalues above 1.0; the first resembles a size vector with mixed loadings, while components 2 and 3 were uninterpretable.

nodes.title: Strontium Isotope Analysis
nodes.summary: Strontium isotope analysis of human tooth enamel, bone, soil and fauna from the Gobero site complex (Sahara) to assess residential mobility. Covers lab methods (ASU, SrSpec resin, MC-ICP-MS, SRM-987 standard, U and Nd contamination proxies). Baseline soil (0.71290) and fauna (0.71261) match preliminary human enamel (0.71189), suggesting local residence versus lower-ratio volcanic Air/Hoggar areas. Also includes figure captions on felsite knapping at Alallaka, a mid-Holocene midden, and mid-Holocene pollen spectra, plus a table of convergent AMS radiocarbon dates from bioapatite of several burials and a cattle sample.

nodes.title: Pollen Analysis
nodes.summary: Describes pollen analysis of 59 samples from 23 Gobero burials (methods: chemical preparation, Lycopodium spike, microscopy), with early, mid-Holocene findings on vegetation: grass-dominated savanna, desert and Sahelian taxa, wet-environment indicators, charcoal, and a mosaic xeric-wet landscape. Also covers Table 7 principal component loadings for North African human samples, Table 8 strontium isotope (87Sr/86Sr) results from human enamel, fauna and soil baselines, Table 9 pollen sampling locations, plus acknowledgments, author contributions, and references.

summary: Covers the Gobero site in Niger: discovery and 2005–2006 excavations of at least 182 burials on paleolake edges, with sieving, mapping and plaster-jacket recovery. Dating uses OSL on paleodune sand and direct 14C AMS on bioapatite. Craniometric PCA compares North African populations across seven units. Strontium isotopes assess mobility. Pollen analysis of 59 samples reconstructs vegetation, plus artifacts, faunal lists and tables.

title: Saharan Lakeside Cemeteries: Isotope Data, Pollen Sampling, Acknowledgments, Contributions
summary: Isotope table listing soil samples from burials G1B17, G1B18, G1B6, G3B23, G3B4, G3B7, G3B9 with 87Sr/86Sr ratios (0.71204–0.71384). Pollen sampling table for three mid-Holocene burials (G1B18, G1B8-10, G3B36) with 13 samples. Discussion of Saharan-to-wet mosaic pollen environment. Acknowledgments thank contributors for figures, comments, photographs, lab analyses, fieldwork. Author contributions list roles by initials across writing, fieldwork, analyses.

title: References
summary: The text is a reference list (items 1-55) from a PLoS ONE article on Saharan lakeside cemeteries. It cites works on Holocene climate and vegetation change in the Sahara and Lake Chad, Megalake Chad, archaeology and prehistory of North and West Africa, sedentism and foraging, fossil fish and human remains, optical and radiocarbon dating, strontium isotope and geochemical sourcing methods, and regional geology.
